title: Meningitis retention syndrome associated with complicated mild encephalitis/encephalopathy with reversible splenial lesion in a young adult patient: a case report
case_prompt: A 32-year-old man with no prior medical history was referred for suspected meningitis after developing fever, headache, urinary retention, and constipation. Seven days before admission he had a sudden fever of 39 °C and received antibiotics the next day. Two days before admission he developed acute urinary retention requiring temporary catheterization. On admission, his temperature was 38 °C. Neurological examination showed nuchal rigidity; he was alert (GCS 15), cranial nerves were intact, motor and sensory exams were normal, deep tendon reflexes were intact, and Babinski signs were absent. He had a mild ataxic gait. Bladder-filling sensation was preserved but he was unable to void; anal sphincter reflex was depressed. Urodynamic studies demonstrated a noncontractile neurogenic bladder. Laboratory studies revealed a normal complete blood count and serum chemistry. Lumbar puncture showed an opening pressure of 240 mmH₂O, 127 mononuclear cells/μL, and a protein concentration of 202 mg/dL; bacterial smears and cultures were negative. CSF interleukin-6 was 18.3 pg/mL, myelin basic protein was 401.5 pg/mL, and oligoclonal bands were negative. Lumbosacral MRI performed on hospital day 4 showed no lesions in the spinal cord. Empiric intravenous acyclovir was started on admission and discontinued on hospital day 9 when CSF PCR for herpes simplex virus type 1 was negative.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Myelitis, Guillain–Barré syndrome, and multiple sclerosis considered but excluded based on the absence of limb sensory disturbances and normal spinal imaging — “Lack of leg numbness and paresthesia, negative for oligoclonal band in the CSF, no occasional lesion on spinal MRI helped us to rule out myelitis, GBS and MS.”  
2. Sacral herpes was considered but deemed unlikely after negative viral testing — “Sacral herpes was also unlikely because HSV DNA was not detected in the CSF.”  
3. The constellation of aseptic meningitis, urinary retention, and constipation is characteristic of meningitis retention syndrome — “Our patient initially presented with acute UT and constipation with aseptic meningitis, which is characteristic of MRS.”
